tldr: No new trading session since Friday 20 Nov's close (markets shut all weekend), but the weekend's incremental evidence widened rather than narrowed Friday's shock: BofA's Global Fund Manager Survey showed the largest cut to tech positioning since June 2006 (52% now expect an AI hyperscaler capex cut within 6 months), and reports surfaced of a separate US probe into Singapore's Megaspeed International over alleged Nvidia chip diversion to China.

Biggest risk to the book, unchanged and reinforced: the owner's ~2.49x-levered silver position is still FAILING its survivability metric (risk sleeve -29.61% off peak, 118% of its 25% tolerance band) with no weekend catalyst to relieve the margin-call-liquidation dynamic -- gold/silver held roughly flat over the weekend (not a further leg down, but not a recovery either).

The Fed chorus hardened, not softened, over the weekend: Dallas Fed's Logan now favors two more hikes beyond December, reinforcing Waller's 50bp 'shock therapy' push for the Dec 8-9 FOMC -- markets price ~90-99% odds of at least a 25bp hike and near-zero odds of a cut.

Crypto had a violent, largely self-contained round-trip: Bitcoin fell to a 2-year low of ~$55,100 (~$2.4-2.7bn liquidated, >90% long) before rebounding 9% to retake ~$60,300 -- net flat-to-up vs Friday but confirming BTC is trading as a high-beta risk proxy to the same shock, not a hedge.

Weekend geopolitics added two live tail-risk threads distinct from the AI/Fed story: Ukraine's reported drone strike on a sanctioned Russian tanker in the Baltic (NATO-adjacent escalation) and ~25 projectile incidents near the Strait of Hormuz in a week, the backdrop Sunday-evening oil futures reopen against.

HK/SG company news was genuinely quiet this weekend (no fresh Tencent/SMIC/Xiaomi/SGX-REIT headlines since Friday's close) -- Monday's Asia open is the first real test of whether Friday's AI-credibility shock and the weekend's broadening fund-manager caution carry through to HK tech and the owner's SGX sleeve.

regime.label: Correction deepens into the weekend: a reinforced hawkish Fed chorus, a violent crypto round-trip, and widening AI-capex-credibility doubt compound Friday's Nvidia/Broadcom shock
regime.oneLiner: The weekend didn't walk Friday's shock back -- a bigger fund-manager-survey tech-positioning cut, a second Nvidia-chip-diversion probe report, and a harder Fed all point the same direction into Monday's open.

topNews.actionable: No direct holding, but this is now a multi-pronged credibility crisis, not a one-headline shock -- raises the odds of AI-capex-narrative contagion into HK tech's own buildout story (0700.HK, 0981.HK) at Monday's Asia open.
